item.content:encoded:
Creepy as all hell initially, but thinking about it … I think this one is my new favorite for including in visionsofabetterworld! So much to go wrong, but so much potential for making the world a better place. In a sense, altruism is already a behavior built on positive reinforcement. We help others because it feels good. This doesn't override our judgement or identities - it just supercharges our empathy. All it asks is that we spread the effect (which is, hypothetically, a good thing).
This has got to be on the short list of SCPs most likely to be breached by "well-meaning" staff. Now that I think of it, I wonder how pervasive infection is inside Manna CF.

I really like this article because it's a parasite that doesn't kill the host. It's creepy because it's unsettling; people don't like brainwashing and cannibalism, people do like altruism, and this parasite makes all of those happen without actually being immediately dangerous. The fact that it lets people keep their inhibitions (Meaning that it never pushes them into killing themselves or anything of the like) also makes it better, since the creepy part is that they feel happy about it.

It's probably my favorite parasite article that I've read on the site just because of how unique the concept is, even if some of the sentence structure is a little odd.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Pointless expungement is when [DATA EXPUNGED] is just thrown in casually as a lazy attempt to make something interesting, there is no build-up to it and it doesn't fit the SCP at all.
Expunged data (in my opinion) should be used for self-replicating memes or things too terrible to even think of (or usually a mixture of the two), this is because that (again, in my opinion) [DATA EXPUNGED] is where the data is completely and utterly deleted due to said reasons but possibly a hard-copy exists somewhere, in a very big safe.
As I can't possibly imagine that this SCP can create any sort of death meme or do something utterly terrible that warrants an expungement it just ruins the entire SCP for me because all I can think of is the person that wrote it did so thinking: "I know, if I put [DATA EXPUNGED] in there rather than writing something actually good then people will try and guess what is behind it!"

Note #1: For proper uses of [DATA EXPUNGED], see SCP-231, SCP-447 and SCP-923.
Note #2: For something that manages to be really mysterious without a single [DATA EXPUNGED], see SCP-055.
